questions.q: In matplotlib, what is an Axes?
options: The x and y number lines only
The file the chart is saved to
A single plot on the canvas, owning its axis lines, title and data
The whole canvas that can hold many plots
questions.explain: The Figure is the whole canvas; an Axes is one plot within it, with its own x-axis, y-axis, title and drawn data.

questions.q: Which line creates a figure and an axes together in the object-oriented style?
questions.explain: plt.subplots() returns a Figure and an Axes, which you then draw on with methods such as ax.plot().

questions.q: Why does this course prefer the object-oriented style over plain plt.plot(...) calls?
options: It is the only way to draw a line chart
It relies on matplotlib remembering the current axes, which keeps code shorter
It stays explicit and clear when a figure holds several charts
questions.explain: The pyplot style depends on an implicit 'current' axes, which becomes confusing with several charts; the object-oriented style names the axes you are drawing on.

questions.q: What does fig.autofmt_xdate() do in the lesson's revenue chart?
options: Rotates crowded date labels so they don't overlap
Saves the figure as a PNG
questions.explain: autofmt_xdate rotates and aligns date tick labels so they stay readable.

questions.q: Which axes method draws a scatter plot of orders against spend?
questions.explain: scatter plots points for two numeric variables; barh draws horizontal bars, hist a distribution and boxplot the spread of groups.
